run.question: My AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 has high latency issues. Investigate why.

report.summary: Requested subject: AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 and its high latency. No AWS/CloudWatch (or any AWS) data source exists in this Run — the available sources are jaeger, knowledge, kubernetes and prometheus against target m0-otel-20260909 (source otel-demo) — and change_history is not integrated. A cross-namespace pod search matching 'payment' or 'lambda' returned no Lambda object and no 'payment-processor' entity; the only payment-named workload is Pod 'payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d' (Deployment 'payment') in namespace otel-demo, which is a different entity. That related workload was checked and showed no latency in the evidence obtainable: flagd fault-injection flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are declared state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off'; payment pod logs from 08:35–08:54Z show each 'Charge request received' followed by 'Transaction complete' within ~1–2 ms; checkout logs show 'payment went through' ~14–30 ms after '[PlaceOrder]'; the payment Service has a ready endpoint pointing at the pod; and the Deployment's ownership chain shows a single ReplicaSet at revision 1, i.e. no pod-template change in the window. All of that concerns the otel-demo in-cluster payment service, not the named Lambda function, and the Lambda latency itself remains unmeasured. One change during the window is recorded but not placed as impact: the kubelet on node opspilot-m1-control-plane logged 'Starting kubelet.' at 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z and every otel-demo pod's sandbox was re-created 08:04:18–08:04:21Z, restarting the payment container (restartCount 2, last termination reason Unknown, exit code 255, current container started 08:04:20Z); whether this relates to the reported latency is unknown. Prometheus and Jaeger tools returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so latency/error-rate series and traces could not be examined at all. Runbook 'lambda-performance-troubleshooting' (skill_id lambda-performance-troubleshooting) was read and each of its steps was checked against available tools: Step 1 (CloudWatch Duration statistics for FunctionName) — not carried out, no CloudWatch/AWS tool and no 'payment-processor' function in any available source; Step 2 (CloudWatch Logs filter for ERROR/WARN/timeout) — CloudWatch Logs unavailable, nearest available analogue carried out instead on pod logs of the otel-demo payment and checkout pods (no error lines among the payment charge/complete lines read; one 'MetadataLookupWarning ... metadata service' line at 08:04:24Z); Step 3 (CloudWatch InitDuration cold-start analysis) — not carried out, CloudWatch unavailable and Lambda has no in-cluster representation; Step 4 (CloudWatch ConcurrentExecutions) — not carried out, CloudWatch unavailable; Step 5 (CloudWatch Logs Insights REPORT maxMemoryUsed/memorySize) — not carried out, Logs Insights unavailable. Assessment: inconclusive, no root cause identified.

claims.text: A cross-namespace pod search matching 'payment' or 'lambda' returned exactly one pod in the whole cluster — 'payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d' in namespace otel-demo, phase Running — and the listing of all 22 otel-demo pods contains no 'payment-processor' pod, so no Lambda-style workload for the named function is represented in this cluster.

The otel-demo payment container was restarted inside the incident window: restartCount 2, lastState.terminated.reason 'Unknown', exit code 255, current running container started at 2026-11-22T08:04:20Z.

Events show 'Starting kubelet.' and NodeAllocatableEnforced on node opspilot-m1-control-plane at 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z with RegisteredNode at 08:04:37Z, and at 2026-11-22T08:04:18Z every otel-demo pod received 'Pod sandbox changed, it will be killed and re-created', followed by container Created/Started events at 08:04:19–08:05:10Z including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d.

ConfigMap 'flagd-config' in namespace otel-demo holds demo.flagd.json in which the payment-specific fault-injection flags are declared state ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off': paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable"); all other flags in that file are likewise defaultVariant 'off'.

The payment Deployment's ownership chain shows a single ReplicaSet 'payment-6f7bc865d6', owner 'payment', deployment.kubernetes.io/revision '1', created 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z with 1/1 ready — no second ReplicaSet or pod-template rollout occurred during the window.

The payment Service in otel-demo (ports tcp-service 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment) has a ready endpoint subset with address 10.244.0.5 pointing at pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, so the service is not short of endpoints.

Against a latency problem in the in-cluster payment service: its own application logs for 2026-11-22T08:35:15Z–08:54:37Z show pairs of 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.' (e.g. trace 4ffcb729f7395758afa4f08f17eefb6e) about 1–2 ms apart, and an error/log-filter pass over the 175 current-instance log lines returned only one line, a Node.js 'MetadataLookupWarning: received unexpected error = Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header' at 08:04:24Z — no charge errors, timeouts or slow operations in the lines read (the log view was incomplete: newest 80 of 173 matching lines shown).

Against caller-observed payment latency: checkout pod logs for 08:50:41Z–08:54:37Z show 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' 14–30 ms after each '[PlaceOrder]' line with 'order confirmation email sent' immediately after, matching the payment transaction_ids (e.g. 1779f1ed-50f6-4dff-a417-8cdbb78938e9), with no error text among the newest 30 of 251 lines returned.

Rejected for the sampled otel-demo payment service: that the flagd payment fault-injection switch was causing payment failures/latency. The two payment-referring flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) are declared with defaultVariant 'off' in the flagd-config ConfigMap read during this Run, and the payment charge calls sampled at 08:35–08:54Z completed normally; this says nothing about the named AWS Lambda function, which is not present in any available source.

The kubelet restart of node opspilot-m1-control-plane at 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z, which re-created every otel-demo pod sandbox (including payment's container at 08:04:20Z), could have caused a transient degradation around that time; no latency measurement is available to confirm or refute this, and nothing ties it to the reported Lambda latency.

If the reported high latency is real, its cause lies in the AWS-hosted Lambda 'payment-processor' (us-east-1) itself or its AWS dependencies (memory/CPU allocation, cold starts, concurrency throttling, downstream AWS service calls), none of which are represented in this cluster — the cluster-wide pod search matched no Lambda workload or 'payment-processor' entity — and none of which could be queried in this Run; confirming this needs CloudWatch Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, Errors/Throttles and that function's CloudWatch Logs.

Run the runbook's CloudWatch steps outside this Run against the real function: get-metric-statistics Duration (Average, Maximum, p99) and InitDuration with dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=payment-processor in us-east-1 over 2026-11-21T08:54:50Z–2026-11-22T08:54:50Z at 300 s period, ConcurrentExecutions at 60 s, and filter-log-events on the function's log group for [ERROR]/[WARN]/timeout plus a Logs Insights REPORT query for @maxMemoryUsed vs @memorySize, so the latency claim, cold-start share and memory pressure can be quantified against a comparable baseline.

Restore the Prometheus (via prometheus-readonly-proxy) and Jaeger paths and then re-check the in-cluster payment service with latency series such as rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} plus payment traces, so the 08:04:14Z kubelet restart can be tested rather than left as coincidence.

gaps: No AWS/CloudWatch, AWS Lambda or CloudWatch Logs data source is available in this Run (only jaeger, knowledge, kubernetes, prometheus on target m0-otel-20260909 / source otel-demo; change_history is listed as not integrated), so Lambda Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, memory usage, throttles and the function's logs for 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 could not be queried at all — the runbook's steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 had no tool to execute them with.

Nothing was found under the exact name 'payment-processor' in any available source: a cross-namespace pod search matching 'payment' or 'lambda' returned only the differently named otel-demo in-cluster workload 'payment' (Pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d), which is a different entity and is not evidence about the Lambda function.

Every Prometheus tool call in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, get_metric_names for traces_*/rpc_*/http_*, metrics_range_query of increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"}[1h]), execute_prometheus_instant_query of sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"}[5m])), get_prometheus_target for job 'prometheus'), and every Jaeger call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services, traces_search for service payment over both windows), so no latency, error-rate or trace evidence could be read; these are unknown, not zero.

The trigger of the 2026-11-22T08:04:14Z kubelet restart on opspilot-m1-control-plane, and whether it degraded latency, is unknown; no change-history source is integrated to show who or what caused it.

Payment pod logs exist only from 2026-11-22T08:04:24Z onward (current container instance started 08:04:20Z, previous instance produced no readable lines), so the earlier part of the authorized window is not covered by application logs; the payment log view was incomplete (newest 80 of 173 matching lines) and the checkout log view was incomplete (newest 30 of 251 lines).
A checkout log filter for 'error|fail|timeout|deadline' returned a no_data view (0 of 254 lines matched) which cannot be cited either way; a wider error survey of checkout was not performed.
Runtime flagd state beyond the ConfigMap defaults (e.g. any live flagd override) was not observable; only the stored demo.flagd.json defaultVariant values were read.
next_steps: Query CloudWatch in us-east-1 for FunctionName=payment-processor: Duration (Average, Maximum, p99), InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, Errors, Throttles and ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization across the incident window and a comparable pre-incident baseline, to establish whether latency deviates and whether cold starts or throttling dominate.

Pull the function's CloudWatch Logs (log group /aws/lambda/payment-processor) with filter-pattern "[ERROR] OR [WARN] OR timeout" and a Logs Insights REPORT query for max(@maxMemoryUsed) vs @memorySize, and review the function's configured memory, timeout, layers and runtime, since memory pressure and small allocations are a common Lambda latency cause.

Check the function's upstream AWS dependencies (e.g. DynamoDB/SQS/S3/other Lambda calls, VPC-attached ENI cold starts, NAT/egress) for latency during the same window, because a slow dependency would surface as Lambda Duration while its own logs stay clean.

If the question is actually about the in-cluster otel-demo payment service, restore Prometheus/Jaeger first: without rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} and payment traces, in-cluster latency cannot be measured and the 08:04:14Z kubelet restart stays an untested coincidence.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.
view.incomplete_reason: limit: the newest 30 of 251 matching lines are shown

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

content.content:
# AWS Lambda High Latency Troubleshooting

## Overview
This runbook helps diagnose and resolve AWS Lambda function performance issues including high latency, timeouts, and cold starts.

## Steps

### Step 1: Query Performance Metrics
Use CloudWatch to check Lambda function latency over time:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name Duration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 2: Check Function Logs
Look for errors or slow operations in CloudWatch Logs:
```bash
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --filter-pattern "[ERROR] OR [WARN] OR timeout" --limit 100
```

### Step 3: Analyze Cold Start Patterns
Query CloudWatch for cold start frequency:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name InitDuration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Count --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 4: Check Concurrent Executions
Verify Lambda isn't hitting concurrency limits:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name ConcurrentExecutions --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 60
```

### Step 5: Review Memory Utilization
Check if function needs more memory allocation:
```bash
aws logs insights start-query --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --start-time <epoch-start> --end-time <epoch-end> \
  --query-string "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @type = 'REPORT' | stats max(@maxMemoryUsed), avg(@memorySize)"
```
